summary: unhappy-path UP-1 (spoofable created_by sentinel via untrusted import, already disclosed in ADR-0058 as a known residual), UP-2 (a single unresolvable legacy-row conflict causes repeated whole-file boot-refusal with no per-row skip tooling), UP-5/sre finding 2 (schedule_runner's per-tick audit write during sustained degradation competes for the same shared PG pool the outage is already starving, plausibly amplifying it). chaos-injector designed 9 fault-injection scenarios and explicitly recommended NOT blocking this PR on any of them (self-healing, bounded, or architecturally out of scope — the shared-pool pattern predates this migration). Not fixed this round; NOT a policy floor since none of these are I1/I2-with-no-mitigation/catastrophic-invariant violations. Deferred to a follow-up hardening issue per chaos-injector's own scope-decision recommendation, bundling CH-2/CH-3/CH-5/CH-6 (per-row backfill skip tooling + audit-amplification circuit breaker) — not yet filed, pending operator decision on whether/how to file.

no Prometheus alert rule exists for yuzu_server_instruction_backfill_total{result=failed}, the read/write-degrade families, or the schedule-fire-failure counter — every new/touched failure-mode signal from this migration is dashboard-only today, requiring an operator to be actively watching. Not fixed this round (requires threshold/on-call judgment calls beyond a mechanical doc/code fix); deferred, not yet filed as a tracked issue.

Targeted re-verify of the 3-commit fix round (849cf6a34/48562a397/0bacdd750) closing findings fullgov-2 through fullgov-7. All six requested verification items independently re-derived from source. Confirmed: exact 7-site audit-vocab fix count both directions, zero remaining denied+degrade-reason pairs; delete_set audit addition correct and create_set genuinely untouched; dispatch_instruction split logically correct and unreachability claim independently traced through run()'s startup_failed_ gate; metric reason values match exactly both directions including the read-degrade and backfill_total families not previously spot-checked; the GET export 200-vs-404 doc correction verified independently correct against source; new tests confirmed non-vacuous via inline-check tracing. Two NICE-tier coverage notes (degrade-counter test bypasses boot registration; no route-level audit-string regression test) — neither a defect.

Operator-directed scope change, not a governance finding: per ADR-0009's fresh-start-by-default class and the ResponseStore (#2691) precedent, InstructionStore's entire legacy-SQLite backfill mechanism was removed post-governance-approval (migrate_from_sqlite, its legacy-table-reading/fingerprint helpers, the sqlite_backfill_source marker table, the 9 [backfill]-tagged regression tests, the dedicated ops-runbook, and all backfill-specific doc/ADR sections) — no production fleet has ever run a pre-Postgres build of any Yuzu store. The claimed ADR-0009 amendment was NOT found in origin/dev at the time of the request; this was surfaced to the operator directly (with the actual ResponseStore precedent text, which is narrower-scoped than the request implied) before proceeding, and the operator explicitly confirmed: 'Take my word for it.' The deleted_seed_content tombstone/every-boot-reseed-loop mechanism (a separate, unrelated concern protecting against a different hazard) is UNAFFECTED and remains fully in place. Verified clean: full rebuild + full server suite green (13/13 shards) post-removal; comprehensive grep sweep across code/docs/changelog confirmed no dangling references to the removed mechanism outside of accurate historical/retirement notes.
waiver_rationale: operator explicit directive, cited authority (ADR-0009 amendment) not independently verifiable in-repo at time of request; operator confirmed intent to proceed regardless after the discrepancy was raised
